1	# Shared Technical Standards
2	
3	Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
8	
9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
10	
11	| Banned Feature | Description |
12	|----------------|-------------|
13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
14	| `mask` | Masks |
15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
30	
31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
32	|---------------|---------------------|
33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
37	
38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference
43	
44	### Presentations
45	
46	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
47	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
48	| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
49	| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |
50	
51	### Social Media
52	
53	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
54	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
55	| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
56	| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
57	| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
58	
59	### Marketing Materials
60	
61	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
62	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
63	| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
64	| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
65	| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
66	| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
71	
72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
84	
85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
86	
87	```bash
88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
90	
91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
93	
94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
97	```
98	
99	**Prohibited**:
100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
103	
104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
109	
110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
111	
112	### Shadow
113	
114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
115	
116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
117	
118	```xml
119	<defs>
120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
125	    <feMerge>
126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
128	    </feMerge>
129	  </filter>
130	</defs>
131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
132	```
133	
134	Recommended parameters:
135	```
136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
139	dx:             0–2
140	```
141	
142	#### Colored Shadow
143	
144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
145	
146	```xml
147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
152	  <feMerge>
153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
155	  </feMerge>
156	</filter>
157	```
158	
159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
160	
161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
162	
163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
164	
165	```xml
166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
170	<!-- Main card -->
171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
172	```
173	
174	### Image Overlay
175	
176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
177	
178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
187	  </linearGradient>
188	</defs>
189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
190	```
191	
192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
195	
196	```xml
197	<defs>
198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```
205	
206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
207	
208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
209	
210	```xml
211	<defs>
212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
215	  </radialGradient>
216	</defs>
217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
218	```
219	
220	#### Brand Color Overlay
221	
222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
223	
224	```xml
225	<defs>
226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
229	  </linearGradient>
230	</defs>
231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
232	```
233	
234	### Quick-Reference Table
235	
236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 7. Project Directory Structure
248	
249	```
250	project/
251	├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
252	├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
253	├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
254	├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
255	│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
256	├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
257	└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
258	```
259

# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

### Quick-Reference Table

| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

---

## 7. Project Directory Structure

```
project/
├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
```

# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

### Quick-Reference Table

|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

---

## 7. Project Directory Structure

```
project/
├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)

```

172	```
173	
174	### Image Overlay
175	
176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
177	
178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
187	  </linearGradient>
188	</defs>
189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
190	```
191	
192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
195	
196	```xml
197	<defs>
198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```
205	
206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
207	
208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
209	
210	```xml
211	<defs>
212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
215	  </radialGradient>
216	</defs>
217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
218	```
219	
220	#### Brand Color Overlay
221	
222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
223	
224	```xml
225	<defs>
226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
229	  </linearGradient>
230	</defs>
231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
232	```
233	
234	### Quick-Reference Table
235	
236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |
244

258	```

1	# Executor Common Guidelines
2	
3	> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Template Adherence Rules
8	
9	If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:
10	
11	| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
12	|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
13	| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
14	| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
15	| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
16	| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
17	| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |
18	
19	### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)
20	
21	Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:
22	
23	```
24	📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
25	🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
26	```
27	
28	- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
29	- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)
34	
35	> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.
36	
37	Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.
38	
39	**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Execution Guidelines
44	
45	- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
46	- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
47	- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
48	- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
49	  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
50	  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
51	- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules
52	
53	### SVG File Naming Convention
54	
55	File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`
56	
57	- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
60	- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 4. Icon Usage
65	
66	Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)
67	
68	**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:
69	
70	```xml
71	<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
72	```
73	
74	> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.
75	
76	**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`
77	
78	> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.
79	
80	Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 5. Chart Reference
85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.
87	
88	**Adaptation rules**:
89	- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
90	- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
91	- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline
93	
94	> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
109	
110	**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 7. Font Usage
115	
116	Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:
117	
118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
119	|------|--------------------|--------------------|
120	| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143	
144	> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.
145	
146	**Requirements**:
147	
148	- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory
151	
152	### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files
153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.
155	
156	**File naming convention**:
157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## 9. Next Steps After Completion
164	
165	> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.
166	
167	**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):
168	
169	```bash
170	# 1. Split speaker notes
171	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
172	
173	# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
174	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
175	
176	# 3. Export PPTX
177	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
178	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
179	```
180	

<system-reminder>
Whenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.
</system-reminder>

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml

```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
60	- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 4. Icon Usage
65	
66	Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)
67	
68	**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:
69	
70	```xml
71	<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
72	```
73	
74	> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.
75	
76	**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`
77	
78	> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.
79	
80	Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 5. Chart Reference
85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.
87	
88	**Adaptation rules**:
89	- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
90	- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
91	- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline
93	
94	> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
109	
110	**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 7. Font Usage
115	
116	Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:
117	
118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
119	|------|--------------------|--------------------|
120	| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143	
144	> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.
145	
146	**Requirements**:
147	
148	- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory
151	
152	### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files
153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.
155	
156	**File naming convention**:
157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## 9. Next Steps After Completion
164	
165	> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.
166	
167	**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):
168	
169	```bash
170	# 1. Split speaker notes
171	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
172	
173	# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
174	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
175	
176	# 3. Export PPTX
177	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
178	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
179	```
180

But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.

### 2. Chart Color Conventions

Consulting-style charts use **monochromatic depth gradients** rather than rainbow colors:

### 3. Data Annotation Principles

### MECE Decomposition Tree

```

|------|---------------------|------------------------|

# TIOBE Index March 2026 - Design Spec

## I. Project Information

| Item | Value |
| ---- | ----- |
| **Project Name** | TIOBE Index March 2026 |
| **Canvas Format** | PPT 16:9 (1280×720) |
| **Page Count** | 6 |
| **Design Style** | B) General Consulting |
| **Target Audience** | Software engineering leads and technology strategists planning language adoption |
| **Use Case** | Data analysis report presentation |
| **Created Date** | 2026-04-20 |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
| -------- | ----- |
| **Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280×720 |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Margins** | Left/right 60px, top/bottom 40px |
| **Content Area** | 1160×640 |

---

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Style**: General Consulting
- **Theme**: Dark cover + light content pages
- **Tone**: Data-forward, analytical, professional

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Purpose |
| ---- | --- | ------- |
| **Background (cover)** | `#0F1B2D` | Cover/closing dark background |
| **Background (content)** | `#FFFFFF` | Content page background |
| **Secondary bg** | `#F1F5F9` | Card backgrounds, table zebra rows |
| **Primary** | `#1565C0` | Title decorations, key sections, headers |
| **Accent** | `#E65100` | Data highlights, negative trends, warnings |
| **Secondary accent** | `#2E7D32` | Positive trends, growth indicators |
| **Body text** | `#1E293B` | Main body text |
| **Secondary text** | `#64748B` | Captions, annotations |
| **Tertiary text** | `#94A3B8` | Supplementary info, footers |
| **Border/divider** | `#E2E8F0` | Card borders, divider lines |
| **Success** | `#2E7D32` | Positive indicators (green) |
| **Warning** | `#C62828` | Negative indicators (red) |

### Gradient Scheme

```xml
<linearGradient id="titleGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1565C0"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#0D47A1"/>
</linearGradient>
```

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Plan

**Recommended preset**: P5 (English-primary)

| Role | English | Fallback |
| ---- | ------- | -------- |
| **Title** | Arial | Helvetica, sans-serif |
| **Body** | Calibri | Arial, sans-serif |
| **Code** | Consolas | Monaco |
| **Emphasis** | Arial Black | Arial Bold |

### Font Size Hierarchy

**Baseline**: Body font size = 18px (dense content — 6+ data points per page)

| Purpose | Ratio | Size | Weight |
| ------- | ----- | ---- | ------ |
| Cover title | 2.5x | 45px | Bold |
| Page title | 1.7x | 30px | Bold |
| Subtitle | 1.3x | 24px | SemiBold |
| **Body content** | **1x** | **18px** | Regular |
| Table/chart text | 0.8x | 14px | Regular |
| Annotation | 0.75x | 14px | Regular |
| Source/footer | 0.6x | 11px | Regular |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

- **Header area**: y=40 to y=90, page title + thin accent bar
- **Content area**: y=100 to y=680, main content
- **Footer area**: y=690 to y=720, source attribution + page number

### Common Layout Modes

| Mode | Used In |
| ---- | ------- |
| Single column centered | Cover (Slide 01), Closing (Slide 06) |
| Full-width table | Top 20 Rankings (Slide 02), Historical (Slide 04), Hall of Fame (Slide 05) |
| Two-column split | Biggest Movers (Slide 03) — gainers left, losers right |

### Spacing Specification

| Element | Value |
| ------- | ----- |
| Card gap | 24px |
| Content block gap | 30px |
| Card padding | 20px |
| Card border radius | 8px |
| Icon-text gap | 10px |

---

## VI. Icon Usage Specification

### Source

- **Built-in icon library**: `templates/icons/` (640+ icons)
- **Usage method**: Placeholder format `<use data-icon="name" .../>`

### Approved Icon List

| Purpose | Icon Name | Page |
| ------- | --------- | ---- |
| Growth/positive | `arrow-trend-up` | Slides 02, 03 |
| Decline/negative | `arrow-trend-down` | Slides 02, 03 |
| Chart/data | `chart-bar` | Slide 02 |
| Timeline | `chart-line` | Slide 04 |
| Trophy/award | `trophy` | Slide 05 |
| Star/highlight | `star` | Slide 05 |
| Target/strategy | `target` | Slide 06 |
| Lightbulb/insight | `lightbulb` | Slide 06 |
| Warning | `triangle-exclamation` | Slide 03, 06 |
| Globe | `globe` | Slide 01 |
| Checkmark | `circle-checkmark` | Slide 06 |

---

## VII. Chart Reference List

| Chart Type | Reference Template | Used In | Purpose |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------- |
| horizontal_bar_chart | `templates/charts/horizontal_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 02 | Top 20 language ranking by rating |
| butterfly_chart | `templates/charts/butterfly_chart.svg` | Slide 03 | Gainers vs losers visual contrast |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List

No images — this is a pure data report.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Slide 01 - Cover

- **Layout**: Dark background, centered title
- **Title**: TIOBE Index March 2026: How 20+ Search Engines Rank the World's Programming Languages
- **Subtitle**: A data-driven analysis of programming language popularity trends for technology decision-makers
- **Info**: TIOBE Programming Community Index | March 2026 | Source: tiobe.com

### Slide 02 - Top 20 Rankings

- **Layout**: Full-width table with integrated horizontal bar indicators
- **Title**: Python Holds #1 at 21.25% but C Surges to #2 with the Largest Gain
- **Takeaway**: The top 4 languages (Python, C, C++, Java) hold 48.97% of the total index
- **Content**: Full 20-row table: Rank, Prior Rank, Language, Rating %, YoY Change with color-coded arrows
- **Source**: TIOBE Index, March 2026

### Slide 03 - Biggest Movers

- **Layout**: Two-column split — left (gainers, green), right (losers, red)
- **Title**: Perl Jumps 13 Spots, R Climbs 7, and Go Drops 9 -- The Biggest Rank Shifts of 2026
- **Takeaway**: Legacy languages show surprising resilience while Go suffers its sharpest decline
- **Content**:
  - Left column (Risers): Perl 24→11 (+1.05%), R 16→9 (+0.94%), Swift 26→20 (+0.44%), C 4→2 (+2.02%)
  - Right column (Fallers): Go 7→16 (-1.49%), C++ 2→3 (-2.90%), Java 3→4 (-2.37%), Python 1→1 (-2.59%)
- **Source**: TIOBE Index, March 2026

### Slide 04 - Historical Trends

- **Layout**: Full-width table with rank position heatmap across decades
- **Title**: From Lisp at #2 in 1986 to Python at #1 in 2026: How Language Rankings Shifted Over Time
- **Takeaway**: C is the only language in the top 2 across all nine measurement points spanning four decades
- **Content**: Long-term ranking table: Python, C, C++, Java, C#, JavaScript, Go, Ada, Lisp across 1986–2026
- **Key patterns**: Python unranked→#1 over 25 years; Java peaked at #1 then declined; Lisp fell from #2 to #26
- **Source**: TIOBE Index Very Long Term History

### Slide 05 - Hall of Fame

- **Layout**: Timeline-style display of winners 2016–2025
- **Title**: Python Wins Language of the Year 6 Times -- More Than Any Other Language
- **Takeaway**: Python dominates with 6 wins; C# took 2023 and 2025; 2017 data not available
- **Content**: Year-winner pairs from 2016 to 2025 with Python wins highlighted
- **Source**: TIOBE Programming Language Hall of Fame

### Slide 06 - Takeaways

- **Layout**: Card grid (2×2 or structured list)
- **Title**: The Top 4 Languages Hold 49% of the Index: What This Means for Your Tech Stack
- **Takeaway**: Concentration risk + opportunity in rising legacy languages
- **Content**:
  - Python dominant but declining (-2.59pp YoY) — watch the trajectory
  - C's resurgence (+2.02pp) and Go's sharp fall (-1.49pp) — systems programming landscape shifting
  - Legacy language revival (Perl, R, Fortran) — entrenched communities in scientific computing and infrastructure
  - Concentration risk: top 4 = 49% — diversify language investments
- **Source**: TIOBE Index, March 2026 Key Findings

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

- **File naming**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.md`)
- **Total duration**: ~8 minutes
- **Notes style**: Professional, conclusion-first consulting tone
- **Presentation purpose**: Inform and advise

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Must Follow:

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` (`<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN)
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`; `rgba()` FORBIDDEN
5. FORBIDDEN: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. FORBIDDEN: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Arrows use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>`

### PPT Compatibility Rules:

- `<g opacity="...">` FORBIDDEN; set on each child element individually
- Inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` FORBIDDEN

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-generation

- [x] Content fits page capacity
- [x] Layout mode selected correctly
- [x] Colors used semantically

### Post-generation

- [ ] viewBox = `0 0 1280 720`
- [ ] No `<foreignObject>` elements
- [ ] All text readable (>=14px)
- [ ] Content within safe area
- [ ] Colors conform to spec

---

## XIII. Next Steps

1. ✅ Design spec complete
2. **Next step**: No AI images → Invoke **Executor** role to generate SVGs

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Header accent bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="#1565C0"/>

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="60" y="42" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">The Top 4 Languages Hold 49% of the Index: What This Means for Your Tech Stack</text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="60" y="56" width="1160" height="28" rx="4" fill="#1565C0" fill-opacity="0.06"/>
  <text x="74" y="75" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#1565C0">Actionable implications for hiring, training, and tooling investments based on March 2026 TIOBE data.</text>

  <!-- Card 1: Python -->
  <defs>
    <filter id="shadow1" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
      <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6"/>
      <feOffset dx="0" dy="3" result="offsetBlur"/>
      <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.06" result="shadowColor"/>
      <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
      <feMerge>
        <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
        <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
      </feMerge>
    </filter>
  </defs>

  <rect x="60" y="100" width="560" height="230" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#shadow1)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="100" width="560" height="6" rx="3" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-bar" x="80" y="120" width="24" height="24" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <text x="114" y="140" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">Python: Dominant but Declining</text>
  <text x="80" y="170" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">21.25% rating -- more than double the #2 language.</text>
  <text x="80" y="192" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">However, -2.59pp YoY is the largest drop among the top 5.</text>
  <rect x="80" y="210" width="520" height="40" rx="6" fill="#F1F5F9"/>
  <use data-icon="lightbulb" x="94" y="220" width="18" height="18" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <text x="120" y="235" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">Action: Continue Python investment, but monitor the trajectory.</text>
  <text x="80" y="275" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Watch if C and other languages continue closing the gap.</text>
  <text x="80" y="295" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Diversify critical infrastructure beyond a single language.</text>

  <!-- Card 2: Systems Programming -->
  <rect x="660" y="100" width="560" height="230" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#shadow1)"/>
  <rect x="660" y="100" width="560" height="6" rx="3" fill="#E65100"/>
  <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="680" y="120" width="24" height="24" fill="#E65100"/>
  <text x="714" y="140" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">Systems Space: C Surges, Go Falls</text>
  <text x="680" y="170" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">C gained +2.02pp (4th to 2nd). Go lost -1.49pp (7th to 16th).</text>
  <text x="680" y="192" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Rust holds steady at 14th (+0.09pp) -- possible Go displacement.</text>
  <rect x="680" y="210" width="520" height="40" rx="6" fill="#FBE9E7"/>
  <use data-icon="target" x="694" y="220" width="18" height="18" fill="#E65100"/>
  <text x="720" y="235" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#E65100">Action: Re-evaluate Go-centric strategies; watch Rust adoption.</text>
  <text x="680" y="275" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Go's sharpest-ever decline contrasts with its 2016 peak.</text>
  <text x="680" y="295" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">C's resurgence reflects embedded and systems-level demand.</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Legacy Revival -->
  <rect x="60" y="350" width="560" height="230" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#shadow1)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="350" width="560" height="6" rx="3" fill="#2E7D32"/>
  <use data-icon="arrow-trend-up" x="80" y="370" width="24" height="24" fill="#2E7D32"/>
  <text x="114" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">Legacy Language Revival</text>
  <text x="80" y="420" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Perl: 24th to 11th (+1.05pp). R: 16th to 9th (+0.94pp).</text>
  <text x="80" y="442" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Fortran holds top 15. These serve entrenched communities in</text>
  <text x="80" y="464" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">scientific computing, data analysis, and infrastructure.</text>
  <rect x="80" y="478" width="520" height="40" rx="6" fill="#E8F5E9"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-checkmark" x="94" y="488" width="18" height="18" fill="#2E7D32"/>
  <text x="120" y="503" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#2E7D32">Action: Don't abandon legacy language expertise prematurely.</text>
  <text x="80" y="543" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Niche communities can drive surprising resurgence.</text>
  <text x="80" y="563" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Maintain skill pipelines for Perl/R/Fortran where applicable.</text>

  <!-- Card 4: Concentration Risk -->
  <rect x="660" y="350" width="560" height="230" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#shadow1)"/>
  <rect x="660" y="350" width="560" height="6" rx="3" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-bar" x="680" y="370" width="24" height="24" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <text x="714" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">Concentration Risk: Top 4 = 48.97%</text>
  <text x="680" y="420" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Python (21.25%) + C (11.55%) + C++ (8.18%) + Java (7.99%)</text>
  <text x="680" y="442" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">account for nearly half the entire index, despite 50+</text>
  <text x="680" y="464" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">tracked languages. High concentration = high dependency risk.</text>
  <rect x="680" y="478" width="520" height="40" rx="6" fill="#F1F5F9"/>
  <use data-icon="lightbulb" x="694" y="488" width="18" height="18" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <text x="720" y="503" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">Action: Diversify language investments across your portfolio.</text>
  <text x="680" y="543" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Align hiring with multi-language strategy: core + emerging.</text>
  <text x="680" y="563" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Track Swift (re-entered top 20) and Rust (steady climb).</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <text x="60" y="700" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#94A3B8">Source: TIOBE Index, March 2026 Key Findings  |  tiobe.com</text>
  <text x="1190" y="700" font-family="Calibri, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#94A3B8">6 / 6</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome to this analysis of the TIOBE Programming Community Index for March 2026. This index measures programming language popularity based on search-engine hit counts across Google, Bing, Wikipedia, Amazon, and over 20 other sites -- it reflects how much a language is discussed and sought after on the public internet. [Pause]

Today we'll walk through the current rankings, the most dramatic movers, four decades of historical context, and what all of this means for your technology strategy.

Key points: (1) TIOBE index measures language discussion volume, not code quality (2) Data sourced from 20+ search engines (3) Focus on actionable implications for tech leaders
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_top_20_rankings

[Transition] Let's start with the current state of the landscape -- the full top-20 rankings for March 2026.

Python holds the top position at 21.25%, more than double the rating of second-place C. But here's the headline: Python posted a year-over-year decline of 2.59 percentage points -- the largest drop among the top five. [Data] Meanwhile, C surged from 4th to 2nd with a +2.02 point gain, the largest positive swing in the top 5. [Pause]

The concentration is striking: Python, C, C++, and Java together account for nearly 49% of the total index. That's half the world's programming language discussion concentrated in just four languages out of more than 50 tracked.

Key points: (1) Python dominant at 21.25% but declining (2) C surges to #2 with +2.02pp (3) Top 4 languages hold 48.97% of total index
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_biggest_movers

[Transition] Now let's zoom in on the most dramatic rank shifts -- the languages that moved the most in the past year.

On the risers side, the standout story is legacy language resilience. Perl jumped 13 spots from 24th to 11th, gaining over one full percentage point. R climbed seven spots from 16th to 9th. Swift re-entered the top 20, climbing from 26th to 20th. And C's surge from 4th to 2nd represents the largest absolute rating gain. [Pause]

On the fallers side, Go suffered its sharpest decline ever -- dropping from 7th to 16th, losing 1.49 percentage points. [Data] That's nine rank positions lost in a single year. C++ and Java also slipped one rank each, continuing their multi-year declines. Python, despite holding #1, posted the largest rating drop in the top 5.

Key points: (1) Legacy languages Perl and R show surprising comeback (2) Go's -9 rank drop is the most dramatic fall (3) Possible Go-to-Rust displacement in systems programming
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 04_historical_trends

[Transition] To put these movements in perspective, let's look at the very long-term view -- four decades of language rankings.

The table spans 1986 to 2026, and it reveals just how dramatically the landscape can shift. Python was unranked before 1991 and sat at 26th as recently as 2001. It took 25 years to climb from obscurity to the number-one position. [Pause]

Contrast that with Lisp, which was the number-two language in 1986 and has fallen to 26th. Or Ada, which peaked at 3rd in 1986 and now sits at 14th. [Data] The one constant: C has remained in the top 2 across all nine measurement points -- the only language with that distinction over four decades.

Java's arc is particularly instructive: it dominated from 2005 to 2018 at number one, but has steadily declined from over 25% to under 8%.

Key points: (1) C is uniquely resilient -- top 2 for 40 years (2) Python's rise took 25 years (3) Today's dominant language may not be tomorrow's
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 05_hall_of_fame

[Transition] The TIOBE Hall of Fame gives us another lens -- which languages gained the most in a given year.

Python has won the Language of the Year award six times -- in 2007, 2010, 2018, 2020, 2021, and most recently 2024. That's more than any other language. [Pause]

C# has emerged as a notable contender, winning in both 2023 and 2025, reflecting continued growth driven by the .NET ecosystem. An interesting contrast: Go won in 2016, but now sits at 16th -- a reminder that a single-year surge doesn't guarantee sustained momentum.

Note that the 2017 winner is not available in our source data.

Key points: (1) Python: 6 wins, all-time record (2) C# won twice recently on .NET strength (3) Go's 2016 win now followed by its sharpest decline
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 06_takeaways

[Transition] So what does all of this mean for your technology strategy? Here are four actionable takeaways.

First, Python remains the safe bet for now at 21.25%, but its declining trajectory warrants monitoring. Don't assume today's dominance is permanent -- the historical data shows us how quickly leaders can change. [Pause]

Second, the systems programming landscape is shifting. C's resurgence and Go's sharp fall suggest re-evaluation of Go-centric infrastructure strategies. Keep an eye on Rust as a potential beneficiary.

Third, don't dismiss legacy languages. Perl and R's dramatic jumps remind us that entrenched communities in scientific computing and infrastructure can drive surprising comebacks.

Finally, with the top four languages holding nearly half the index, there's real concentration risk. [Data] Roughly one in two language discussions on the internet involves just Python, C, C++, or Java. Diversifying your language portfolio is a prudent hedge.

Key points: (1) Monitor Python's decline trajectory (2) Re-evaluate Go investments; watch Rust (3) Maintain legacy language capabilities (4) Diversify to reduce concentration risk
Duration: 2 minutes
